what: Transaction amount in USD
motivation: Fraudsters monetize stolen cards with goods they can resell
if_higher: Larger than usual raises risk when other tells agree; size alone is weak
if_lower: A few dollars can be a probe charge (card testing)

what: Amount divided by this customer's median amount over the prior 90 days
catches: account takeover, counterfeit card and dormant-card cash-outs
motivation: Fraud is judged against the customer's own habits, not the population
if_higher: Far above 1: spending well beyond this customer's norm
if_lower: Far below 1: unusually small for this customer; with velocity it suggests card testing

what: Amount divided by this customer's 95th-percentile amount over the prior 90 days
motivation: Above 1 means bigger than almost anything this customer has bought
if_higher: Above 1: an outlier purchase for this customer

what: 1 if the amount is under 5 USD
motivation: Fraudsters check stolen cards with small charges before cashing out

what: 1 if the amount is a multiple of 10 USD
motivation: Kept as a control; round amounts are common for legit fuel

what: Amount divided by the population median for this merchant category
motivation: Puts the amount in the context of what people usually pay at this kind of merchant
if_lower: Below 1: cheap for the category; tiny values at digital merchants fit card testing

what: Card transactions in the last 10 minutes, including this one
motivation: Testing scripts fire many attempts within minutes

what: Card transactions in the last hour, including this one
motivation: Bursts of attempts within an hour

what: Card transactions in the last 24 hours, including this one
catches: card testing, dormant-card and takeover sprees
motivation: Fraud compresses spending into a short window
if_higher: Well above the customer's usual daily count

what: Distinct merchants used in the last hour
motivation: Testers hop across merchants to find one that approves

what: Charges under 5 USD in the last hour
motivation: Several probe-sized charges in an hour is the classic testing pattern

what: Spend in the last 24 hours divided by this customer's average daily spend
motivation: Captures a sudden surge in total spend
if_higher: Above 5: a day of spending far beyond normal

what: Minutes since the customer's previous card transaction
catches: card testing (very short gaps); dormant reactivation (very long gaps)
motivation: Both extremes matter: machine-speed bursts and long silences

what: Transactions in the last 7 days divided by the customer's average weekly count
motivation: Detects activity bursts relative to habit

what: Distance between the transaction location (or the IP location for online) and the customer's home
catches: counterfeit card; takeovers from far away
motivation: Cloned cards are used where the fraudster is, not where the customer lives
if_higher: Hundreds of km: far from home; check travel history

what: Distance from the previous transaction's location
motivation: A card can't be in two distant places within hours
if_higher: Large with a short time gap: impossible travel

what: Distance from the previous transaction divided by the time between them
motivation: Speeds above about 900 km/h are physically impossible; 200 to 900 needs a flight

what: 1 if the physical card was swiped or dipped
catches: counterfeit card, when far from home
motivation: A physical card far from home suggests a cloned card

what: Distinct 100-km regions with transactions in the last 24 hours
motivation: A card used in several regions in one day is suspicious
if_higher: 2 or more: several regions in a day

what: Share of this customer's in-person transactions over the prior 90 days that were more than 200 km from home
motivation: Travelers are often far from home; homebodies rarely are
if_higher: High: a frequent traveler, so distance is less alarming
if_lower: Near 0: never travels, so a distant swipe is alarming

what: Local hour of the transaction, 0 to 23
motivation: Context; its meaning depends on the customer's routine

what: 1 if between 00:00 and 04:59
motivation: Takeovers often happen while the owner sleeps

what: Share of this customer's prior 90-day transactions that were NOT within 2 hours of this hour (0 = their usual hour, 1 = never at this hour)
motivation: Fraudsters don't know the owner's routine
if_higher: Near 1: this customer never transacts at this hour

what: 1 on Saturday or Sunday
motivation: Kept as a control

what: Longest gap between consecutive transactions in the prior 90 days, including the gap that ends now
motivation: A card silent for weeks that suddenly spends may be compromised
if_higher: Above about 30 days: the card was dormant

what: 1 if card not present (online)
catches: account takeover, card testing, dormant reactivation
motivation: Most takeovers and testing happen online

what: 1 if this online transaction comes from a device never seen for this customer
motivation: A fraudster uses their own device

what: Days since this device was first seen for this customer (online only)
motivation: New devices are riskier than long-trusted ones

what: Distinct online devices for this customer in the last 30 days
motivation: A second device appearing suddenly can mean someone else is in the account

what: Days since the last change of email, phone or password (999 = never)
motivation: Takeovers change contact details first to lock the owner out
if_lower: Small (days): a recent credential change, a takeover tell

what: Age of the card account in days
motivation: New accounts are riskier on average

what: 1 if email, phone or password changed in the last 7 days
motivation: Same signal as days_since_profile_change, as a flag

what: Fraud risk of the merchant category (0 = low, 3 = high: digital goods, electronics, jewelry)
motivation: Fraudsters prefer goods that are easy to resell

what: 1 if the customer never used this merchant before
motivation: Fraud happens at merchants the owner doesn't use

what: 1 if the customer never bought in this category before
motivation: Unfamiliar categories suggest a different person

what: Transactions at this merchant across all customers in the last 30 days
catches: card testing and cash-outs at obscure shops
motivation: Obscure merchants are where testers and cash-outs cluster

what: 1 if the merchant sells digital goods (gift cards, game credits)
motivation: Digital goods are instant and resellable

what: Share of this customer's prior 90-day transactions in this category
motivation: Buying in a category the owner rarely uses
if_lower: Near 0: a category this customer rarely buys

what: Customer's transactions in the prior 30 days
motivation: A quiet card that suddenly spends
if_lower: Near 0: the card was quiet for a month

what: Days with at least one transaction in the prior 90 days
motivation: Low recent activity makes a burst stand out

what: Customer's median transaction amount over the prior 90 days
motivation: Baseline for the amount ratios

what: Share of the customer's prior 90-day transactions that were online
motivation: Online fraud stands out for customers who rarely shop online
if_lower: Near 0: rarely online, so online activity is unusual

what: Customer's total prior transactions in the data
motivation: Thin histories make baselines unreliable
if_lower: Small: a thin history, so baselines are noisy
